A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CEDAR research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 17 models, emotion-bias and prompt-language analyses, and human annotation agreement results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds narrative-refinement and translation audits plus an evaluation incorporating minority emotion labels.

M1.justification: The generation, refinement, filtering, clustering, and majority-label construction procedures remain unchanged, including the construction prompts. The new Top-2 analysis changes auxiliary evaluation rather than the benchmark construction method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 10,962 CEDAR instances across seven languages and 14 emotions, with 400 multimodal and 1,166 text-only instances per language. The added analyses use retained benchmark material.

E2.justification: The 17 evaluated models and their documented versions are unchanged. New Table 5 reuses Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen2-VL-72B, Claude4.5-Sonnet, and GPT-4o under an additional evaluation protocol; existing comparisons retain their participants.

E3.justification: v2 adds Top-2 ground-truth evaluation using Macro F1 for four models and two 100-instance human audits, including two 10-point translation-rating scales. Main evaluation settings remain unchanged. Appendix B identifies 6,477 instances with valid minority labels but leaves their exact handling within the scoring population unclear.

E4.justification: New targeted analyses test whether refinement removes explicit emotion cues while preserving meaning, whether translations preserve context and fluency, and whether language disparities persist when minority labels are included. Existing annotation-agreement, emotion-bias, and prompt-language analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly states that all p-values are below 0.01, without identifying the test or tested comparisons. Existing cross-language variances and annotation-agreement statistics remain unchanged; no repeated-run or confidence-interval procedure is added.

E6.justification: v2 adds 93% successful narrative refinement, translation scores of 9.16/10 for factual consistency and 9.36/10 for fluency, and 28 Top-2 Macro F1 entries, including GPT-4o's 0.759 in English. Earlier numerical results are unchanged. The additional scores use different evaluation conditions and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical task definition, EPP and RQB formulas in Equations 1–2, and Russell quadrant mapping are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution, evaluation scope, and headline claims about emotional biases and the dissociation between language consistency and cultural alignment retain their meaning in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly recognizes valid minority emotion labels and interprets persistent language disparities under Top-2 scoring as robustness to the majority-label choice. It also interprets translation ratings as evidence of contextual preservation. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes reported code and data availability from forthcoming to available. Conversely, Section 2.5 drops explicit target-region recruitment wording, and Ethical Considerations removes compensation, consent, and withdrawal disclosures. These are documentation changes; actual recruitment changes are not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fleisig et al. (2023) on annotator disagreement and several LLM and affective-computing references, with a brief expansion of Section 5.1. The cultural-benchmark comparison and central novelty positioning remain unchanged. Updated GPT-4o and Qwen3 citations identify the same underlying works.

P1.justification: Changes include limited prose additions, new translation-validation and multi-label subsections, appendix renumbering, acknowledgments, and revised author/contact information. Most explanatory text and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Top-2 results table and relocates retained appendix tables. Figures 9–10 change from small side-by-side prompt panels to larger vertically stacked panels. Existing result figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new audits provide direct evidence for refinement and translation quality that v1 only described, while the minority-label analysis adds a useful sensitivity check. Larger prompt panels improve readability. These gains are limited by underexplained Top-2 scoring and significance testing, together with reduced annotator documentation; the principal results and conclusions remain unchanged.
